categories.main_business_segments: As of the end of 2021, First Citizens BancShares, Inc. operated as a single segment but, following the CIT Group merger in January 2022, it plans to report three operating segments: General Banking (retail and small business banking, wealth management), Commercial Banking (lending, leasing, advisory, factoring, supply chain finance), and Rail (equipment leasing and secured financing to railroads and shippers), plus a non-operating Corporate segment.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: FCNCA relies on a combination of traditional branch banking, digital banking platforms, remote image technology for business customers, and a robust IT infrastructure for transaction processing and risk management. The company has invested in automation, digital enhancements, and technology upgrades to improve efficiency, customer experience, and operational resilience, including cybersecurity and data protection measures.
categories.primary_customers_markets: The company serves a broad range of customers including individuals, small businesses, middle-market companies, and professionals. Key end markets include retail banking, commercial lending (across industries such as healthcare, industrials, real estate, technology, and transportation), wealth management, and specialty finance (factoring, equipment leasing, and supply chain finance).
categories.geographic_coverage: FCNCA operates primarily in the United States, with a branch network spanning 19 states as of 2021, including major presences in North Carolina, South Carolina, and California. The CIT merger expanded its footprint, especially in Southern California, and added some international exposure through railcar leasing in Canada and Mexico.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates as a downstream provider in the financial services supply chain, delivering end products and services directly to consumers, businesses, and institutions. In specialty finance (e.g., factoring, equipment leasing), it also acts as a financial intermediary supporting the working capital and asset needs of commercial clients.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: FCNCA’s strategic priorities include growth through mergers and acquisitions, digital transformation, operational efficiency, and expansion of noninterest income streams. The company is focused on integrating CIT, enhancing technology and digital delivery, optimizing its branch network, and developing new products and services to meet evolving customer needs, with an emphasis on risk management and regulatory compliance.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through net interest income from loans and leases, as well as noninterest income from fees (wealth management, service charges, cardholder and merchant services, mortgage origination, insurance commissions, and gains on securities). Additional revenue streams include equipment leasing, factoring, and advisory services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: FCNCA competes with national, regional, and local banks (notably Bank of America, Truist, and Wells Fargo in its core markets), as well as non-bank financial service providers and fintechs. Post-CIT merger, it is a top 20 U.S. bank by asset size, with strong positions in North Carolina and South Carolina (4th largest by deposits), and a growing national commercial lending and specialty finance presence.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, FCNCA had $58.3 billion in assets, $51.4 billion in deposits, and $528.9 million in net income available to common shareholders. The CIT merger (closed January 2022) more than doubled its asset base to over $100 billion, positioning it for further growth and subjecting it to enhanced regulatory standards. The company has demonstrated steady profitability and capital strength, with a 10.7% increase in net income in 2021.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: FCNCA emphasizes a full-service banking model combining personalized service, a broad product suite, and digital convenience. Its value proposition includes strong local market knowledge, a robust retail and commercial banking franchise, specialized industry expertise (e.g., healthcare, rail, factoring), and a commitment to operational stability, risk management, and community investment. The CIT merger enhances its scale, product breadth, and ability to serve a wider range of clients nationwide.
